report:
Perianal fistula tract, excision

Received in formalin are irregular pieces of tan-brown soft tissue labelled fistula tract, measuring 2.5 x 1 x 0.8 cm in aggregate. All embedded in 2 blocks.

(1-2) Tissue pieces, all embedded.

Sections show perianal skin and subcutaneous tissue with a tract lined by inflamed granulation tissue, with surrounding mixed acute and chronic inflammatory infiltrates and fibrosis. Non-necrotising epithelioid granulomas are present. No acid-fast bacilli are identified on Ziehl-Neelsen stain. No fungal organisms are identified on PASD stain. The features are consistent with fistula-in-ano. There is no evidence of malignancy.

PERIANAL, fistula tract, excision - Consistent with FISTULA-IN-ANO; non-necrotising granulomas present; see comment

Granulomatous inflammation is present. The differential diagnosis includes Crohn's disease, mycobacterial infection including tuberculosis, and hidradenitis suppurativa. Correlation with the clinical and microbiological findings is suggested.
